name: Optimize qni-webgpu GitHub Actions CI runtime

description: Baseline projected CI critical path from the current single-job workflow using latest successful Actions setup timings plus fresh local check durations.

asi.hypothesis: Current single-job CI serializes web, mcp, and tui checks behind two expensive cargo-install setup steps, so job topology is the highest-leverage first optimization.
asi.next_action_hint: Try splitting the workflow into parallel jobs that separate trunk/web setup from cargo-audit-deny/tui setup.

description: Split the single CI job into parallel web, mcp, and tui jobs while preserving the same validation commands, and enabled pnpm cache/frozen-lockfile installs for the Node jobs.

asi.hypothesis: Breaking the workflow into independent jobs should overlap the expensive trunk install and cargo-audit-deny install instead of serializing them behind one critical path.
asi.workflow_strategy: parallelize web/mcp/tui jobs with direct per-job commands
asi.next_action_hint: Validate the projected win against a fresh local review, then explore faster Rust tool installation or caching for the remaining dominant web/tui setup steps.

description: Replace cargo-install-based trunk and cargo-audit/cargo-deny setup with taiki-e/install-action prebuilt binaries and add rust-cache to web/tui jobs.

asi.hypothesis: Prebuilt Rust tool installers plus rust-cache should collapse the remaining trunk and cargo-audit/cargo-deny setup bottlenecks without changing validation coverage.
asi.proxy_limit: projected_ci_s still uses old fixed setup timings and now materially overestimates real CI after switching installer strategy.
asi.next_action_hint: Recalibrate the proxy to current workflow timings, prune tried ideas, then explore smaller remaining setup wins such as folding wasm target install into toolchain setup or stabilizing required-check aggregation only if it preserves runtime.

description: Tried combining BDD and legacy Playwright under one shared trunk server in the web job via a new test:ci-web runner and Playwright external-server mode.

asi.hypothesis: Running BDD and legacy Playwright against one pre-started trunk server should avoid duplicated web-server bootstrap and reduce the web job critical path.
asi.rollback_reason: The projected metric regressed slightly and the combined local web command was slower than the current separate commands, so there is no evidence this orchestration pays for its added complexity.
asi.next_action_hint: Revert the shared-server web runner and try a lower-risk setup optimization next, such as folding the wasm target into rust-toolchain setup or recalibrating the proxy to current CI timings before chasing smaller wins.
asi.notes: BDD already reuses an external server when one exists, but adding a combined CI-only runner plus Playwright external-server mode did not produce a measurable local improvement.

description: Fold the web job's wasm32 target install into dtolnay/rust-toolchain so CI drops the standalone rustup target step while keeping the same toolchain setup.

asi.hypothesis: Installing wasm32-unknown-unknown through dtolnay/rust-toolchain should remove one dedicated setup step from the web job and slightly shorten the critical path without changing validation coverage.
asi.workflow_strategy: merge wasm target provisioning into Setup Rust for the web job
asi.next_action_hint: Push this keep and inspect the real CI run; if the gain is marginal, the next promising lane is recalibrating the proxy to the post-install-action workflow or caching Playwright/browser setup.

name: Optimize qni-webgpu GitHub Actions CI runtime (recalibrated proxy)

description: Recalibrate the CI runtime proxy to seed per-step costs from the latest successful branch run instead of stale cargo-install-era timings.

asi.hypothesis: Using the latest successful CI run as the proxy seed should keep future local experiments aligned with post-install-action reality, especially for topology changes that duplicate formerly expensive setup steps.
asi.benchmark_change: projected_ci_s now derives observed step durations from the latest successful branch CI run and falls back to local timings or legacy constants only when no observed step exists.
asi.next_action_hint: Now that the proxy reflects current CI shape, try splitting the web suites into parallel jobs; the actual bottleneck is 74s BDD + 48s legacy inside one 168s web job.

description: Split the web validation lane into parallel web-bdd and web-legacy jobs so the two longest web suites overlap instead of serializing inside one job.

asi.hypothesis: Now that setup is cheap, duplicating the web job setup should cost less than serializing the 74s BDD suite and 48s legacy Playwright suite behind one critical path.
asi.workflow_strategy: parallelize the two web suites into separate jobs while keeping the same commands and coverage
asi.next_action_hint: Push this change and compare the real CI wall clock against run 25157172723; if branch protection needs a stable web check name, add a tiny aggregate job only after measuring the pure speed win.

description: Add a web-build artifact job that runs trunk build once, then serve the built dist to parallel web-bdd and web-legacy jobs so the expensive cold compile is not repeated inside legacy Playwright.

asi.hypothesis: If the split-web regression comes from redoing a 54.9s trunk compile inside the isolated legacy job, building dist once and reusing it via artifact should preserve parallelism while removing the cold compile from both test jobs.
asi.root_cause_evidence: Run 25157503984 showed web-legacy spent 54.92s compiling qni-egui-web before tests, while the warmed single-web legacy step in run 25157172723 compiled in ~0.15s and finished the suite in 44.9s.
asi.workflow_strategy: centralize trunk build in web-build, upload dist, then run BDD and legacy against a static http.server with Playwright external-server mode
asi.next_action_hint: Push and validate against real CI; if wall clock improves, consider a tiny aggregate web status job only if required-check naming becomes a problem.

name: Optimize qni-webgpu GitHub Actions CI runtime (dependency-aware proxy)

description: Make the CI runtime proxy dependency-aware by computing the longest path through workflow job needs instead of assuming every job runs fully in parallel.

asi.hypothesis: A dependency-aware proxy should stop overestimating wins from workflows that insert serial build jobs before downstream test jobs.
asi.benchmark_change: projected_ci_s now sums per-job durations along the longest needs chain, not just the max standalone job duration.
asi.next_action_hint: Use this new 160s baseline to evaluate a single-web-job static-dist hypothesis, which may keep one compile while avoiding the serial web-build bottleneck.

description: Tried collapsing back to one web job that builds dist once and then runs BDD plus legacy against the static output, avoiding trunk serve inside both suites.

asi.hypothesis: A single static-dist web job might keep one compile while removing the serial web-build → web-legacy chain and duplicated browser/dependency setup.
asi.rollback_reason: Under the dependency-aware proxy this came out slightly worse than the current artifact-split baseline, so there is not enough evidence to justify another real CI run yet.
asi.next_action_hint: Return to the slower-but-measured artifact split baseline and try a smaller verified win next, such as reducing per-web-job Playwright browser install cost or adding queue-aware telemetry before exploring topology again.
asi.notes: This candidate likely trades serial dependency overhead for a larger single web job, but the current model does not show a win.

description: Remove the explicit Playwright Chromium install from web-bdd and web-legacy so both jobs reuse the runner's preinstalled system browser through the shared browser policy.

asi.hypothesis: Because ubuntu-latest already ships a system Chrome/Chromium, teaching the plain-browser path to resolve that binary should let both web test jobs skip the 12s Playwright browser install step entirely.
asi.root_cause_evidence: The shared browser policy already prefers system Chrome for standard mode, and runner-images documentation plus existing command lookup logic indicate ubuntu-latest exposes Chrome in PATH; only the plain-browser path still forced Playwright's downloaded defaultPath.
asi.workflow_strategy: use system-installed browser for both standard and plain modes, eliminating explicit playwright install steps from the split web artifact workflow
asi.next_action_hint: Push and validate on real CI; if the runner truly has the browser preinstalled, this should cut ~24s from the artifact-split path and may finally beat the earlier 168s warmed single-web run.

description: Keep the system-browser Playwright hypothesis, but fix the browser-launch preflight contract so plain mode still falls back to bundled Chromium when no system browser exists.

asi.hypothesis: Skipping explicit Playwright installs remains promising if plain mode prefers a system browser when available but still preserves the bundled fallback contract for environments without Chrome in PATH.
asi.root_cause_evidence: Run 25158549124 failed in web-build preflight, not in CI runtime behavior: browser-launch.test expected plain mode to always use the bundled Chromium, but the new helper intentionally preferred system Chrome when present.
asi.actual_ci_failure: web-build preflight test mismatch in browser-launch.test.cjs
asi.next_action_hint: Push the repaired keep and re-run real CI to measure whether removing explicit Playwright installs lowers the artifact-split workflow below the previous 199s wall clock.

name: Optimize qni-webgpu GitHub Actions CI runtime (history-aware dependency proxy)

description: Make the dependency-aware proxy history-aware by averaging step-name timings across several recent successful branch runs while keeping exact job/step timings from the latest success.

asi.hypothesis: A history-aware proxy should evaluate workflow shapes more honestly by reusing empirical timings for step names seen in older successful topologies instead of falling back to misleading warm local command durations.
asi.benchmark_change: projected_ci_s now seeds exact job-step durations from the latest successful branch run and step-name averages from the latest five successful branch runs.
asi.next_action_hint: Use this 150s baseline to evaluate a warmed single-web workflow with no explicit Playwright install; the proxy can now borrow historical Web Cucumber BDD / Web Playwright legacy timings from earlier successful runs.

description: Tried reverting to a single warmed web job with no explicit Playwright browser install, letting BDD warm the trunk compile before legacy Playwright runs.

asi.hypothesis: With system-browser fallback in place, the old single-web topology might regain its warmed-compile advantage and beat the split artifact workflow without paying any Playwright install cost.
asi.rollback_reason: The history-aware proxy still modeled this topology as slower than the current artifact-based branch, so there is not enough evidence to spend another real CI run here.
asi.next_action_hint: Return to the artifact-based no-browser-install baseline and explore smaller wins that preserve the current 180s actual wall clock, such as reducing web-build trunk build cost or artifact overhead.
asi.notes: The proxy can now see historical single-web timings, and those were not strong enough to offset the loss of parallelism against the current branch baseline.

name: Optimize qni-webgpu GitHub Actions CI runtime (history-aware proxy with local command timings)

description: Use local command timings for modeled test steps and make the legacy Playwright suite parallel-safe so fullyParallel can reduce the web test runtime without fixed screenshot-path collisions.

asi.hypothesis: If modeled test steps use fresh local command timings instead of stale historical durations, the proxy can see real gains from enabling fullyParallel once the legacy Playwright suite stops sharing fixed /tmp screenshot paths.
asi.benchmark_change: Command-like workflow steps now use fresh local measurements first; observed CI history remains the source of truth for non-command setup steps and fallback timing.
asi.root_cause_evidence: Legacy Playwright was stuck on one worker and shared hard-coded /tmp screenshot paths; after switching to testInfo.outputPath and fullyParallel, local web runtime dropped from ~15.3s to ~7.3s.
asi.next_action_hint: Push and validate on real CI; if the web-legacy step actually drops in the artifact workflow, compare the new wall clock against the current 180s branch run and then decide whether another topology change is still needed.

description: Collapse the no-browser artifact workflow into one static-dist web job so trunk build happens once and BDD plus legacy run serially against the same built output without artifact fan-out.

asi.hypothesis: Now that legacy is parallel-safe and the explicit browser install is gone, a single static-dist web job should be faster than the artifact fan-out because it avoids upload/download plus downstream job startup while still paying the trunk build only once.
asi.root_cause_evidence: The current best actual run 25159226468 still spends 84s in web-build and then another 63s in downstream web-legacy; collapsing those into one warmed job removes the serial artifact boundary.
asi.workflow_strategy: single web job with preflight -> trunk build -> BDD static dist -> legacy static dist, plus unchanged mcp/tui parallel jobs
asi.next_action_hint: Push and validate on real CI; if actual wall clock drops below 162s, compare against the old warmed-trunk 168s run and consider stopping or only chasing the remaining 55s trunk build cost.

description: Configure Swatinem/rust-cache with explicit subdirectory workspaces for apps/egui-web and apps/tui so cache discovery uses the real Cargo roots instead of failing cargo metadata at repo root.

asi.hypothesis: The current Rust cache restore is partially blind because both web and tui jobs run in a repo without a root Cargo.toml; pointing rust-cache at the real subproject workspaces should let it restore and save the correct target directories, reducing trunk build and tui check time on CI without changing coverage.
asi.root_cause_evidence: Successful CI run 25159433581 shows both web and tui Cache Rust artifacts steps invoking `cargo metadata --all-features --format-version 1 --no-deps` at `/home/runner/work/qni-webgpu/qni-webgpu` and erroring with `could not find Cargo.toml`, while the actual Cargo projects live under `apps/egui-web` and `apps/tui`.
asi.workflow_strategy: keep the current single static-dist web topology and only fix rust-cache workspace discovery for the two Rust-backed jobs
asi.benchmark_caveat: The projected metric only moves slightly because local command timings dominate the proxy, but this candidate specifically targets a CI-only cache miss visible in GitHub Actions logs.
asi.next_action_hint: Push and validate on real CI; if wall clock improves, inspect how much Web trunk build and TUI check dropped, then decide whether the next lane is residual trunk build cost or stopping at the new best actual runtime.

description: Force the legacy Playwright suite to use 4 workers on CI so the warmed static-dist web job no longer serializes all 13 legacy browser tests behind Playwright’s default 1-worker CI cap.

asi.hypothesis: Playwright defaults to 1 worker on CI even with fullyParallel enabled, so explicitly setting a modest CI worker count should materially reduce the remaining 45s legacy step without changing test coverage or browser policy.
asi.root_cause_evidence: Warm-cache rerun 25159979620 still printed `Running 13 tests using 1 worker` and spent 45.1s in `Web Playwright legacy (static dist)`. A local CI-like static-dist run showed the same suite dropping from 11.9s at `--workers=1` to 5.1s at `--workers=4`, while still passing.
asi.verification: Added a failing config test asserting CI uses 4 workers, made it pass, reran `pnpm -C apps/egui-web run test:preflight`, and reran a CI-like static-dist legacy suite with `CI=1` plus the external server; all passed and the legacy suite reported `Running 13 tests using 4 workers` with 13/13 passing.
asi.benchmark_caveat: The big projected metric drop also reflects the newly warmed cache-aware observed CI run 25159979620 from the previous workspace fix. Real CI validation is still needed to isolate the incremental effect of the worker change itself.
asi.next_action_hint: Push and validate on GitHub Actions with warmed caches; if the web job drops meaningfully below 100s, inspect whether any further work beyond this point is worth the added complexity.

description: Tried raising the CI-only Playwright worker cap from 4 to 6 for the warmed static-dist legacy suite.

asi.hypothesis: If the remaining 4-worker legacy suite is still underutilizing the runner, nudging CI to 6 workers might shave a few more seconds off the 42s legacy step without destabilizing the suite.
asi.root_cause_evidence: A local CI-like static-dist run improved from 4.2s at 4 workers to 3.7s at 6 workers, but the already-pushed 4-worker CI run only reduced the legacy step from 45.1s to 42.2s, so the expected incremental gain was modest.
asi.verification: Updated the config test to require 6 CI workers, reran the targeted config test, reran `pnpm -C apps/egui-web run test:preflight`, and reran a CI-like static-dist legacy suite; all passed and the local legacy run reported `Running 13 tests using 6 workers` with 13/13 passing.
asi.rollback_reason: The projected metric regressed slightly after incorporating the latest observed 4-worker CI run, and the expected real-world gain over 4 workers looks too small to justify another push/run right now.
asi.next_action_hint: Revert to the validated 4-worker setting and investigate higher-leverage remaining costs instead, especially Rust toolchain/setup overhead and the residual wasm-bindgen download inside the warmed web build.

description: Drop dtolnay/rust-toolchain from the warmed PR workflow and rely on the runner’s preinstalled Rust toolchain, keeping only an explicit wasm32 target add in web.

asi.hypothesis: Warm-cache PR runs are now paying mostly for rustup refreshing stable from the runner’s already-installed toolchain. Removing the explicit toolchain action should save roughly 10-12s on the critical web path and another ~11s on tui while preserving the same checks.
asi.root_cause_evidence: Run 25160458002 showed `Setup Rust` spending 12s in web and 11s in tui. The web log also showed the runner already had Rust 1.94.1 plus components installed, and dtolnay/rust-toolchain spent its time syncing stable, removing the old components, downloading six components, and upgrading to 1.95.0 before the actual job work began.
asi.workflow_strategy: use the preinstalled Rust toolchain on ubuntu-latest, add only `rustup target add wasm32-unknown-unknown` for the web job, and leave the warmed rust-cache/static-dist topology otherwise unchanged
asi.risk: This trades explicit rust-toolchain refreshes for the runner image’s bundled stable toolchain. Because rust-toolchain.toml only requests `stable` plus fmt/clippy and not an exact patch version, the main risk is slightly looser patch freshness rather than a validation-coverage change.
asi.next_action_hint: Push and validate on real CI. If the runner already has everything needed, the warmed branch wall clock should drop below the current 94s. If it fails or regresses, restore explicit toolchain setup and focus on residual wasm-bindgen/web legacy cost instead.

description: Teach the CI runtime proxy to measure local warmed `trunk build` time explicitly so wasm-bindgen and web-build optimizations are visible instead of being hidden behind stale observed CI step durations.

asi.hypothesis: The current proxy is blind to the remaining web-build bottleneck because it does not locally measure `Web trunk build`, so trunk/wasm-bindgen improvements can look neutral or worse until after an expensive real CI run.
asi.root_cause_evidence: On warmed CI rerun 25160767677, `Web trunk build` was only ~5s and clearly dominated by non-compile overhead, but the proxy still had to borrow historical observed step timings instead of a fresh local build measurement. Local warmed `trunk build` currently completes in ~1.5s, which is a much better predictor for follow-up web-build experiments than the old fallback.
asi.benchmark_change: `autoresearch.sh` now measures warmed local `env -u NO_COLOR TRUNK_COLOR=never trunk build` in `apps/egui-web`, emits `web_trunk_build_s`, and uses that timing when modeling the `Web trunk build` workflow step.
asi.next_action_hint: Use the new benchmark visibility to test caching Trunk-managed wasm-bindgen artifacts next; that is now the clearest remaining web critical-path target.

description: Tried adding an explicit GitHub Actions cache for Trunk-managed tool downloads under ~/.cache/trunk in the web job.

asi.hypothesis: Caching `~/.cache/trunk` should let warmed CI runs skip Trunk's per-run wasm-bindgen download/install and shave a couple more seconds from the web critical path.
asi.root_cause_evidence: Trunk 0.21.14 stores downloaded tools in `ProjectDirs::from("dev", "trunkrs", "trunk").cache_dir()` (Linux: `~/.cache/trunk`) and will use that cache when the required wasm-bindgen version is present. Warm CI logs still show `INFO downloading wasm-bindgen` inside `Web trunk build` after Rust artifacts are restored.
asi.rollback_reason: Under the improved proxy this regressed slightly because local `trunk build` is already fully warm, so the extra cache restore step adds cost while the benchmark cannot observe any further local gain. That makes this a CI-only cache optimization with insufficient proxy evidence to justify another remote run right now.
asi.next_action_hint: Revert this workflow-only trunk cache idea for now. The next higher-signal lane is to prune the stale rust-toolchain idea and either accept the current near-best state or investigate whether a more explicit actual-CI acceptance rule is needed for CI-only cache experiments.

description: Model the web suites in CI-like external-server mode and enable bounded Cucumber scenario parallelism on CI so the proxy reflects the actual static-dist workflow and the BDD lane can overlap its three scenarios.

asi.hypothesis: The proxy should measure the web suites under the same `CI=1` external-server conditions as the workflow, and once it does, giving Cucumber a small CI-only parallelism budget should reduce the BDD step without changing scenario coverage.
asi.root_cause_evidence: `pnpm run test:bdd` locally completed in ~1.9s, but the workflow's static-dist BDD step took ~13s because it runs under `CI=1` with an external server. A local CI-like run against the static dist improved from ~2.67s at `--parallel 1` to ~1.76s at `--parallel 2`, while still passing all 3 scenarios / 13 steps.
asi.benchmark_change: `autoresearch.sh` now measures BDD and legacy under `CI=1` with the same external static-server contract used in GitHub Actions, instead of measuring the looser local default mode.
asi.verification: Added a failing cucumber config test asserting CI uses bounded parallelism, made it pass, reran the targeted cucumber config tests, reran `pnpm -C apps/egui-web run test:preflight`, and reran a CI-like external-server Cucumber run; all passed.
asi.next_action_hint: Push and validate on real CI; if the BDD step drops materially below the current ~13s, inspect whether the current branch finally beats the previous 94s warmed wall-clock run by a convincing margin.

description: Raise the CI-only Playwright worker cap from 4 to 6 now that the proxy measures the legacy suite in CI-like external-server mode.

asi.hypothesis: With the benchmark now exercising the legacy suite under `CI=1` static-dist conditions, raising the Playwright worker cap from 4 to 6 should show whether the remaining ~40s CI legacy step is still underutilizing the runner.
asi.root_cause_evidence: The updated benchmark plus direct CI-like local runs show `playwright test` dropping from roughly 4.2s at 4 workers to about 3.8s at 6 workers against the external static server, while all 13 tests still pass. The earlier discard happened before the proxy could observe CI-like legacy behavior directly.
asi.verification: Updated the CI worker-count config test to fail on the old value, made it pass at 6 workers, reran the targeted Playwright config tests, reran `pnpm -C apps/egui-web run test:preflight`, and reran a CI-like external-server legacy Playwright suite; all passed.
asi.next_action_hint: Push and validate on real CI; if the legacy step falls materially below ~42s and the web job beats the new 88s branch run, keep this lane. If not, revert to 4 workers and stop revisiting worker-count tuning.

description: Make the proxy model `Web trunk build` using cold Trunk tool-cache timings, and distinguish between the current no-system-wasm-bindgen path and a system-wasm-bindgen path for future workflow experiments.

asi.hypothesis: The proxy should model Trunk's wasm-bindgen setup cost under an empty tool cache, because CI runners are ephemeral and the remaining web-build optimization is specifically about avoiding that cold tool download path.
asi.root_cause_evidence: Trunk 0.21.14 first looks for a matching system `wasm-bindgen` on PATH, and only downloads into `~/.cache/trunk` if it cannot find one. Local measurements with an empty `XDG_CACHE_HOME` showed cold `trunk build` taking ~3.26s without a system tool and ~1.42s when a matching `wasm-bindgen` binary was prepended to PATH, which aligns with the CI logs that still show `INFO downloading wasm-bindgen` before an ~8s trunk build.
asi.benchmark_change: `autoresearch.sh` now measures warmed trunk build, cold trunk build with an empty Trunk tool cache, and cold trunk build with a matching system wasm-bindgen on PATH. The workflow model uses the cold-system variant only when the web job explicitly installs wasm-bindgen; otherwise it uses the cold no-system variant.
asi.next_action_hint: Use this improved model to test installing a matching system wasm-bindgen in the web job next; that hypothesis now has a proxy signal grounded in CI-like cold-tool behavior.

description: Install a matching system wasm-bindgen in the web job so Trunk can use PATH discovery instead of downloading wasm-bindgen into its ephemeral tool cache during trunk build.

asi.hypothesis: If the web job installs the exact wasm-bindgen version required by the app, Trunk should find that system binary on PATH and skip its per-run download/install path, shortening the web critical path on ephemeral CI runners.
asi.root_cause_evidence: Trunk's tool resolver first calls `find_system(Application::WasmBindgen)` and only downloads into `~/.cache/trunk` if no matching system version is found. Local cold-cache measurements showed `trunk build` dropping from ~2.86s without a system tool to ~1.40s when a matching `wasm-bindgen` binary was present on PATH.
asi.workflow_strategy: keep the current warmed static-dist topology, but preinstall `wasm-bindgen@0.2.106` in the web job via `taiki-e/install-action@v2` before `trunk build`
asi.benchmark_caveat: This improvement is still proxy-backed, so real CI must confirm that the extra install step is cheaper than Trunk's current download/install path on GitHub-hosted runners.
asi.next_action_hint: Push and validate on real CI; if `Web trunk build` or overall `web` drops below the current best (`web=85s`, run 25161542044), keep it. If not, revert and treat the remaining wasm-bindgen overhead as not worth additional workflow complexity.

description: Tried replacing the system wasm-bindgen install with an explicit GitHub Actions cache for Trunk’s ~/.cache/trunk tools directory in the web job.

asi.hypothesis: Because Trunk stores downloaded wasm-bindgen binaries under ~/.cache/trunk, restoring that directory early in the web job might preserve the same cold-run savings as a system wasm-bindgen install while avoiding an explicit extra tool install step.
asi.root_cause_evidence: The improved proxy can now distinguish no-system cold trunk builds (~3.51s) from warmed/cached tool builds (~1.41s), and the current install-wasm-bindgen branch showed that shaving trunk-build setup alone is not enough if the rest of the web job does not also improve.
asi.rollback_reason: Even under the improved trunk model this candidate projected worse on top of the latest branch evidence, so it is not a strong enough follow-up to justify another real CI run right now.
asi.next_action_hint: Return to the current branch state, then either explicitly unwind the unproven system-wasm-bindgen change or pursue a different web-lane bottleneck with a clearer projected win.

description: Tried reverting the CI-only Playwright worker cap from 6 back to 4 while keeping the current branch workflow otherwise unchanged.

asi.hypothesis: The best actual run with 6 workers only barely beat earlier 4-worker evidence on the legacy step, so returning to 4 workers might reduce browser startup overhead on GitHub-hosted runners while preserving the current workflow shape.
asi.root_cause_evidence: Local CI-like legacy runs still show 6 workers slightly faster than 4 workers, and with the current branch evidence anchored on run 25161888248 the proxy no longer sees a convincing case for rolling back to 4 workers.
asi.verification: Changed the config test to require 4 CI workers, observed the test fail first, updated the Playwright config, reran the targeted config tests, reran `pnpm -C apps/egui-web run test:preflight`, and reran a CI-like external-server legacy Playwright suite; all passed.
asi.rollback_reason: Under the current benchmark and latest branch evidence this regressed materially, so there is not enough signal to justify another real CI run for the 4-worker rollback in isolation.
asi.next_action_hint: Restore the validated 6-worker setting and improve the proxy so it can compare candidate workflows against matching historical CI runs rather than only the latest branch run.

description: Make the proxy select exact observed CI timings from successful runs whose job step names match the current workflow, instead of always seeding from the latest successful branch run.

asi.hypothesis: The proxy should compare a candidate workflow against historical CI runs with the same job-step topology; otherwise a changed workflow can inherit misleading exact timings from an unrelated latest branch run and overfit badly.
asi.root_cause_evidence: Recent experiments showed that actual CI contradicted some proxy wins because the script always seeded exact job-step timings from the latest successful branch run, even when the candidate workflow had different step sets such as `Install wasm-bindgen` or different web-lane structure. Matching on ordered job step names is a stronger invariant for apples-to-apples reuse of exact CI timings.
asi.benchmark_change: `autoresearch.sh` now scans recent successful branch runs, computes a step-name fingerprint per job, and uses the most recent runs whose job step names exactly match the current workflow for exact timings and step averages. It falls back to the latest successful runs only when no exact workflow match exists.
asi.next_action_hint: Re-evaluate the system-wasm-bindgen change against this workflow-aware proxy by removing the explicit install step and seeing whether the model now lines up better with the known better actual run `25161542044`.

description: Tried removing the explicit web-job wasm-bindgen install to unwind the previous system-wasm-bindgen experiment.

asi.hypothesis: Now that the proxy is workflow-aware, removing the explicit system wasm-bindgen install should compare against the historically matching no-install workflow and may realign the branch with the known-better actual run 25161542044.
asi.root_cause_evidence: The attempt exposed a benchmark bug: GitHub's observed job step lists include the synthetic `Set up job` step, but the workflow fingerprint logic compared them directly against YAML-defined steps and therefore found no exact workflow match. The proxy silently fell back to the latest successful branch run instead of the intended matching historical run.
asi.rollback_reason: Cannot trust this result because the workflow-matching benchmark logic was incomplete; fix the synthetic-step matching bug first, then retry the no-install candidate.
asi.next_action_hint: Exclude synthetic steps like `Set up job` from workflow fingerprint matching in `autoresearch.sh`, rerun the benchmark improvement, and then retry the no-system-wasm-bindgen workflow comparison.

description: Fix the workflow-aware proxy to ignore GitHub’s synthetic `Set up job` step when matching historical CI runs against the current workflow step fingerprint.

asi.hypothesis: Exact-workflow matching is only useful if it ignores GitHub-generated synthetic steps that are not present in the YAML; otherwise even truly matching historical runs are misclassified as non-matches.
asi.root_cause_evidence: Direct inspection of `gh run view` showed successful runs like 25161542044 include `Set up job` ahead of all user-defined steps. The initial workflow-fingerprint logic compared those raw step lists against the YAML-defined steps, so no historical runs could ever match exactly.
asi.benchmark_change: `autoresearch.sh` now excludes `Set up job` from the run-side workflow fingerprint before comparing observed runs to the current YAML. This preserves exact matching on real user-defined steps while still allowing synthetic setup time to be modeled separately via fallback/observed step timings.
asi.next_action_hint: Retry the no-system-wasm-bindgen workflow now that the proxy can actually match it against historical run 25161542044 instead of silently falling back to the latest different workflow.

description: Unwind the explicit web-job wasm-bindgen install now that the proxy can compare this workflow against matching historical no-install CI runs.

asi.hypothesis: The previous system-wasm-bindgen keep was a proxy artifact. Once the benchmark compares this candidate against exact historical runs with the same no-install workflow, the branch should realign with the actual best-known CI topology.
asi.root_cause_evidence: After fixing workflow matching, the no-install candidate now correctly selects observed CI run 25161542044 as its exact historical baseline instead of the newer install-wasm-bindgen run 25161888248. That historical no-install run is also the current best actual branch result (`web=85s`, `tui=36s`, `mcp=13s`).
asi.workflow_strategy: retain the current preinstalled Rust / static-dist / Cucumber-parallel / Playwright-6-worker topology, but remove the explicit `Install wasm-bindgen` step and let Trunk manage wasm-bindgen as before
asi.benchmark_caveat: The projected metric only nudges slightly because the primary value here is agreement with real CI evidence, not a large new local speedup.
asi.next_action_hint: Push and validate on real CI. If the branch returns to or beats the known 85s web run, keep the branch aligned to this no-install workflow and stop revisiting system-wasm-bindgen installs.

description: Tried shrinking the shared browser viewport from 1000x800 to 760x560 for both Playwright and Cucumber-driven browser runs.

asi.hypothesis: A smaller shared viewport should reduce screenshot size and pixel-processing cost in the web suites without changing coverage, potentially shaving a few seconds from the web lane.
asi.root_cause_evidence: Local CI-like runs stayed green and the legacy suite improved from about 3.8s to 3.4s at 760x560, while Cucumber remained roughly flat. However the workflow-aware proxy anchored itself to the latest matching observed run 25162727553, which is a slower no-install run than the 85s rerun evidence for the same topology.
asi.verification: Added a failing config test asserting the shared viewport contract, updated the shared viewport in both browser paths, reran the targeted config tests, reran `pnpm -C apps/egui-web run test:preflight`, and reran CI-like external-server Cucumber plus legacy Playwright suites; all passed.
asi.rollback_reason: The projected metric regressed under the current exact-run selection logic, so this is not strong enough to justify a real CI push yet.
asi.next_action_hint: Revert the viewport shrink for now and improve the workflow-aware proxy so matching-run reuse is less sensitive to one slow latest success (for example, use a central tendency across matching runs). Then retry this candidate if it still looks promising.

description: Make the workflow-aware proxy use the median duration across matching historical runs for exact job-step timings instead of trusting the most recent matching run wholesale.

asi.hypothesis: When there are several matching historical CI runs for the same workflow, using the median exact duration per job-step should reduce noise from a single unlucky run and make the proxy less brittle for close-call optimization decisions.
asi.root_cause_evidence: The no-install workflow now has multiple matching successful CI runs with materially different outcomes (for example, 85s reruns and a slower 93s fresh run). Seeding exact timings from only the latest matching run makes the proxy swing with that one sample instead of the broader evidence for the same topology.
asi.benchmark_change: `autoresearch.sh` now collects exact job-step timings across all matching historical runs and uses the median per `[job, step]` pair as well as the median per step name, rather than taking exact timings only from the newest match.
asi.next_action_hint: Re-evaluate close-call web candidates such as the smaller shared viewport under this median-based proxy; it should now be less sensitive to one noisy matching run.

description: Retried shrinking the shared browser viewport from 1000x800 to 760x560 after improving the workflow-aware proxy.

asi.hypothesis: With the proxy now using median timings across matching runs, the smaller shared viewport should get a cleaner comparison and may show a real win if screenshot/pixel-processing cost matters on CI.
asi.root_cause_evidence: Local CI-like suites remained green and the legacy suite again improved modestly (about 3.8s → 3.3s), but even under the median-based workflow-aware proxy the candidate still came out clearly worse than the current branch baseline.
asi.verification: Reintroduced the failing viewport contract test, changed both Playwright and Cucumber browser paths to use the smaller shared viewport, reran the targeted config tests, reran `pnpm -C apps/egui-web run test:preflight`, and reran CI-like external-server Cucumber plus legacy Playwright suites; all passed.
asi.rollback_reason: Still not enough proxy evidence to justify spending another real CI run on a close-call optimization that has already looked marginal twice.
asi.next_action_hint: Revert the viewport change and focus on benchmark integrity or entirely different bottlenecks rather than more micro-tuning of the current web test settings.

description: Make the proxy measure cold Trunk tool-setup paths as the median of three local runs instead of trusting a single network-sensitive sample.

asi.hypothesis: The cold `trunk build` variants are noisy because they include network-backed wasm-bindgen download behavior, so the proxy should take a median across several local cold runs before using those numbers to judge Trunk-tool experiments.
asi.root_cause_evidence: Single-sample cold Trunk measurements swung from roughly 3.2s to 6.7s across nearby runs even when the workflow did not materially change. That kind of variance can distort close-call decisions about no-install versus Trunk-tool setup lanes.
asi.benchmark_change: `autoresearch.sh` now measures both cold Trunk variants (`web_trunk_build_cold_s` and `web_trunk_build_cold_system_wasm_bindgen_s`) as the median of three isolated local runs, while still leaving warmed local commands as single measurements.
asi.next_action_hint: With the cold Trunk measurements stabilized, focus the next experiment on a genuinely different bottleneck rather than more micro-tuning of already-discarded web viewport/worker/cache variants.

description: Tried measuring all local validation commands as medians of three runs instead of single samples.

asi.hypothesis: If the warmed local web, MCP, and TUI commands are also somewhat noisy, taking medians across three runs should make the proxy less brittle for close-call workflow decisions.
asi.root_cause_evidence: The experiment exposed a benchmark harness bug rather than a meaningful metric result: the repeated BDD measurement reused a fixed port (`4174`) and collided with an already-running local server, producing `OSError: [Errno 98] Address already in use` from `python3 -m http.server`. The current single-run benchmark path often got away with that because an existing external server sometimes satisfied the tests anyway, masking the bind failure.
asi.rollback_reason: Cannot trust this experiment result because the measurement harness was flaky under repeated local web-suite runs.
asi.next_action_hint: First harden the benchmark harness so repeated CI-like web-suite measurements use isolated dynamic ports instead of a fixed shared port. Then retry the local-command median idea.
asi.error_detail: Repeated `test:bdd` benchmarking on a fixed port is incompatible with the long-lived local egui-web server expectation and can either fail hard or silently ride on an unrelated existing server.

description: Fix the proxy’s CI-like web-suite benchmark harness so BDD and legacy Playwright actually run from `apps/egui-web` on isolated dynamic ports, then measure local run-step timings as medians of three runs.

asi.hypothesis: The next benchmark-integrity gap was the warmed local run-step sampling: repeated medians should reduce noise, but only after the CI-like web-suite harness is corrected to use isolated ports and a shell structure that actually runs the tests from `apps/egui-web`.
asi.root_cause_evidence: Investigation showed the old web benchmark command had two correctness bugs. First, it reused fixed port `4174`, which collided with the long-lived local egui-web server requirement and could silently piggyback on an unrelated existing server. Second, the `cd ... && python3 ... & ... pnpm run ...` shell structure backgrounded the `cd` together with the server start, so the later `pnpm run test:bdd` / `test:pw-legacy` could execute from the repo root instead of `apps/egui-web`. The corrected harness now uses multiline shell commands, dynamic free ports, and three-run medians; this raised `web_local_s` from an implausible ~1.3s to a believable ~7.9s, confirming the previous local web-step model was under-measuring reality.
asi.benchmark_change: `autoresearch.sh` now measures warmed local commands (`test:preflight`, warmed `trunk build`, BDD, legacy Playwright, MCP check, TUI check`) as medians of three runs. The BDD and legacy measurements now allocate an ephemeral localhost port per run and keep all setup plus `pnpm run` execution inside the intended `apps/egui-web` shell context.
asi.next_action_hint: With the proxy no longer under-measuring local web run steps, re-evaluate hypotheses against this corrected benchmark and avoid spending real CI runs on wins that only exist under the old broken local harness.

description: Raise the CI-only Playwright legacy worker cap from 6 to 7 after the corrected local web benchmark showed a small stable speedup without the flakiness seen at 8+ workers.

asi.hypothesis: The legacy Playwright suite may still have a little unused parallelism beyond the validated 6-worker setting, and 7 workers could be a safe middle ground that preserves stability while shaving a few tenths of a second locally.
asi.root_cause_evidence: After fixing the local web benchmark harness, ad-hoc CI-like legacy runs showed 7 workers consistently finishing around 4.2–4.5s versus roughly 4.4–4.6s for 6 workers. Higher values (8, 10, 12) exposed intermittent test failures and long slowdowns, so the safe search space narrowed to a bounded step up rather than aggressive fan-out.
asi.verification: Changed the config test to require 7 CI workers and observed it fail first, updated `apps/egui-web/playwright.config.cjs`, reran the targeted config test, reran `pnpm -C apps/egui-web run test:preflight`, reran one CI-like BDD suite, and reran the CI-like legacy suite twice against isolated external static servers; all passed.
asi.next_action_hint: Push this 7-worker candidate to real CI next. If the actual `Web Playwright legacy (static dist)` step drops below the current best 45s neighborhood without introducing flakes, keep it; otherwise revert and treat 6 as the stable ceiling.

description: Restore the CI-only Playwright legacy worker cap from 7 back to 6 after real GitHub Actions evidence showed 7 workers made the web job slower overall.

asi.hypothesis: The small corrected-local speedup at 7 workers was likely overfitting to local conditions; restoring 6 workers should realign the branch with the better real-CI behavior once we account for the new actual run.
asi.root_cause_evidence: Real GitHub Actions run `25164375879` on the 7-worker candidate finished successfully but regressed the web job to about 92s overall, with `Web Playwright legacy (static dist)` around 44s and the full workflow wall clock around 107s. That is worse than the validated 85s-best no-install baseline, so actual CI overruled the local-only proxy win. After folding that run back into the benchmark context, the corrected proxy also nudged back toward the 6-worker configuration.
asi.verification: Changed the config test back to require 6 CI workers and observed it fail first, restored `apps/egui-web/playwright.config.cjs`, reran the targeted config test, reran `pnpm -C apps/egui-web run test:preflight`, reran one CI-like BDD suite, and reran one CI-like legacy Playwright suite against isolated external static servers; all passed.
asi.next_action_hint: Treat 6 workers as the current stable ceiling again. Prune the >6-worker lane from the ideas backlog and look for a different bottleneck than raw Playwright worker fan-out.

description: Tried replacing the 50ms post-drag preview settles in the web tests with a single-frame wait helper (`16ms`).

asi.hypothesis: The web test lane still contains about 550ms of fixed 50ms sleeps after drag actions; replacing them with a single-frame settle helper should preserve intent while shaving a noticeable fraction of the local legacy/Bdd runtime.
asi.root_cause_evidence: Targeted CI-like reruns showed the single-frame version was not stable enough. BDD stayed green, but a 3-run legacy sample produced one slow failure (`dragged palette gate keeps rounded corners`) and `./autoresearch.sh` then failed in the repeated `test:pw-legacy` measurement. This indicates at least some drag-preview sampling paths still need more than one extra frame after `dragPointer` before pixel assertions become deterministic.
asi.verification: Added a failing unit test for a shared paint-settle helper, implemented it, rewired the raw 50ms waits through that helper, reran `node --test apps/egui-web/test-node/egui-helpers.test.cjs`, reran `pnpm -C apps/egui-web run test:preflight`, and ran repeated CI-like BDD plus legacy suites against isolated static servers before the full benchmark.
asi.rollback_reason: The single-frame settle overfits to the fast local case and makes the legacy suite flaky under repeated CI-like runs, so it is not safe to benchmark further or push to real CI.
asi.next_action_hint: Let autoresearch revert this change, then either abandon the raw sleep-reduction lane or only retry it with a clearly safer synchronization strategy that preserves determinism rather than blindly shrinking waits.
asi.failure_detail: `./autoresearch.sh` crashed in the repeated `pnpm run test:pw-legacy` benchmark after the 16ms settle change; an earlier manual 3-run sample already showed a 1/3 failure rate for the legacy suite.

description: Tried reducing the egui helper polling interval from 100ms to 50ms for startup/state-vector/canvas readiness waits.

asi.hypothesis: More frequent readiness polling should reduce average slack in the web suite without changing semantics, because the tests could observe app readiness closer to the moment it becomes true.
asi.root_cause_evidence: The tuned interval stayed stable under repeated CI-like BDD and legacy runs, but it did not actually help the warmed local timings: BDD was roughly flat while legacy drifted slightly slower (about 4.6s median versus the current ~4.3s neighborhood). The full proxy also regressed from the current 6-worker/no-install branch state.
asi.verification: Added a failing unit test to lock the intended helper poll interval, updated `apps/egui-web/features/support/egui-helpers.cjs`, reran `node --test apps/egui-web/test-node/egui-helpers.test.cjs`, reran `pnpm -C apps/egui-web run test:preflight`, ran repeated CI-like BDD and legacy suites against isolated static servers, and then ran `./autoresearch.sh`.
asi.rollback_reason: This changed synchronization cadence but produced no real speed win under the corrected benchmark, so it is not worth carrying or validating on real CI.
asi.next_action_hint: Revert the polling-interval tweak and move away from generic wait-tuning. The remaining promising work is either another benchmark-integrity improvement or a materially different CI bottleneck with larger upside.

description: Tried collapsing the sequential static-dist BDD + legacy workflow steps into a single parallel web-suites step that runs both test suites concurrently against one shared static server.

asi.hypothesis: The web critical path is currently the sequential sum of BDD plus legacy after `trunk build`; running those suites concurrently against one shared static server in the same job could cut roughly 2 seconds locally and potentially much more on CI without duplicating setup.
asi.root_cause_evidence: Ad-hoc local measurements showed an attractive median for concurrent execution (~4.8s vs ~6.9s sequential), but repeated verification was not stable enough. A 3-run verification sample failed once in the legacy suite with `page.waitForFunction: Timeout 20000ms exceeded` while BDD was running concurrently, and the full `./autoresearch.sh` run then crashed during repeated legacy measurement. The likely issue is resource contention during simultaneous browser-heavy suites rather than a deterministic command bug.
asi.verification: Added a shared parallel-runner shell script, rewired the workflow and benchmark harness to use it, reran `pnpm -C apps/egui-web run test:preflight`, and ran repeated local parallel suite invocations against isolated static servers before the full benchmark.
asi.rollback_reason: Even though the concurrent lane has upside, the current implementation is too flaky under repeated local CI-like runs to justify keeping or pushing it to real CI.
asi.next_action_hint: Let autoresearch revert this draft. If this lane is revisited, reduce contention explicitly (for example by lowering BDD parallelism only in the concurrent mode or otherwise bounding total browser concurrency) and verify stability before reintroducing the workflow change.
asi.failure_detail: The candidate failed local repeated verification and `./autoresearch.sh`; during parallel verification the legacy suite hit `TimeoutError: page.waitForFunction: Timeout 20000ms exceeded` in `waitForAppReady`, indicating the combined workload can starve browser startup/readiness.

description: Retried the parallel static-dist web-suites lane with explicit Cucumber parallelism forced down to 1 during the concurrent run.

asi.hypothesis: The parallel BDD+legacy lane probably failed because total browser concurrency was too high; forcing Cucumber down to one scenario at a time during the combined run might preserve most of the overlap win while avoiding startup starvation.
asi.root_cause_evidence: Even with BDD parallelism forced to 1, repeated local verification was still flaky. One verification run timed out in the BDD startup scenario (`When the app finishes initializing`), and `./autoresearch.sh` then crashed in the repeated parallel benchmark command. This suggests the contention problem is deeper than Cucumber’s scenario fan-out and likely comes from sharing one runner between simultaneous browser-heavy suites.
asi.verification: Added a failing config test for an explicit Cucumber parallel override, implemented the env-based override, recreated the shared parallel-runner script and workflow/benchmark wiring, reran the targeted cucumber-config test, reran `pnpm -C apps/egui-web run test:preflight`, and ran repeated local parallel-suite invocations against isolated static servers before the full benchmark.
asi.rollback_reason: The contention-reduced variant is still unstable under repeated CI-like runs, so this lane is not safe enough to keep exploring in its current form.
asi.next_action_hint: Let autoresearch revert this draft and prune the same-job parallel web-suites lane for now. Shift back to benchmark integrity or a completely different bottleneck rather than trying to force two browser suites to share one runner concurrently.
asi.failure_detail: Parallel verification with `QNI_EGUI_WEB_CUCUMBER_PARALLEL=1` still produced a 20s BDD startup timeout, and the repeated `web-parallel` benchmark command failed in `./autoresearch.sh`.

description: Tried tightening exact observed-run matching so the proxy only reuses historical CI timings when both the workflow step names and the runtime-relevant tracked files match the current branch state.

asi.hypothesis: Step-name-only workflow matching is still too coarse, because runs like the 7-worker candidate and the restored 6-worker branch share identical job step names while materially differing in runtime-relevant test configuration. Requiring relevant tracked files to match should make exact observed-run reuse less overfit-prone.
asi.root_cause_evidence: Direct inspection showed real CI run `25164375879` (7-worker candidate) and run `25164643080` (restored 6-worker branch) have identical workflow step names, so the current proxy treats them as exact matches even though `apps/egui-web/playwright.config.cjs` and its preflight contract changed between the two commits. That is a benchmark-integrity gap. However the first validation attempt hit an unrelated flaky legacy benchmark run before the new matching logic could produce metrics.
asi.rollback_reason: Cannot judge the benchmark-improvement candidate from this run because `./autoresearch.sh` crashed in a repeated local `test:pw-legacy` measurement unrelated to the new matching logic itself.
asi.next_action_hint: Reapply the runtime-fingerprint matching change and rerun the same benchmark-improvement experiment. The next run needs to confirm that exact-match selection now excludes the 7-worker CI run from the current 6-worker branch state.
asi.failure_detail: The failed `run_experiment` died inside the existing repeated legacy benchmark command; manual reruns immediately after the crash passed 3/3, so this looks like a transient legacy-suite flake rather than evidence against the matching change.

description: Tighten exact observed-run matching so the proxy only reuses historical CI timings when both the workflow step names and the runtime-relevant tracked files match the current branch state.

asi.hypothesis: Step-name-only workflow matching is still too coarse, because runs like the 7-worker candidate and the restored 6-worker branch share identical job step names while materially differing in runtime-relevant test configuration. Requiring relevant tracked files to match should make exact observed-run reuse less overfit-prone.
asi.root_cause_evidence: Real CI runs `25164375879` (7-worker candidate) and `25164643080` (restored 6-worker branch) have identical workflow step names, so the previous proxy treated both as exact matches. However `git diff <run_sha> HEAD -- .github/workflows/ci.yml Makefile scripts/check-all.sh apps/egui-web apps/mcp-qni apps/tui` shows the 7-worker head differs from the current branch in runtime-relevant files (`apps/egui-web/playwright.config.cjs` and its preflight contract), while the current head and the older 6-worker/no-install heads still match exactly.
asi.benchmark_change: `autoresearch.sh` now first looks for successful CI runs whose job step names match the current workflow and whose runtime-relevant tracked files also match the current branch state. Only if no such runs exist does it fall back to step-name-only workflow matching, and only after that to generic recent successful runs.
asi.verification: Validated the new selector logic manually against recent CI history: the current branch now exact-matches runs `25164643080`, `25163578570`, `25162727553`, and `25161542044`, while correctly excluding the 7-worker run `25164375879` despite identical workflow step names. Then reran `./autoresearch.sh` successfully.
asi.next_action_hint: Use this stricter benchmark to re-evaluate future close-call candidates; it should prevent exact observed timings from inheriting runtime from branches that only look identical at the YAML step-name level.

description: When exact runtime-matching CI runs exist, make the proxy use their observed run-step durations directly instead of overriding them with local command timings.

asi.hypothesis: Once the proxy has successful CI runs that match both the current workflow and the current runtime-relevant files, those exact observed step durations should be more trustworthy than local machine timings for the same run steps.
asi.root_cause_evidence: Even after tightening exact-run selection, the proxy still overrode matching CI run-step durations with local command medians for `Web preflight`, `Web trunk build`, `Web Cucumber BDD`, `Web Playwright legacy`, `MCP check`, and `TUI check`. That kept the projected metric artificially low (~30s) despite exact matching real CI evidence around the mid-80s for the current branch state.
asi.benchmark_change: `autoresearch.sh` now prefers observed per-job-step durations for all steps, including `run:` steps, whenever the selected successful runs are exact runtime matches for the current branch state. Only when such exact runtime matches do not exist does it fall back to local command timings for those steps.
asi.verification: Reran `./autoresearch.sh` successfully after the change. The projected metric moved from the unrealistic ~30s range to `82s`, which is much closer to the real CI evidence for the current branch state, and the selector anchored on the latest exact runtime-matching run set (`observed_ci_run_id=25166587211`, `observed_ci_run_count=5`).
asi.next_action_hint: Use this more realistic proxy for the next non-benchmark experiment. With exact runtime matches now consuming observed run-step timings directly, future close-call wins should need less real-CI correction.

description: Tried splitting `Web preflight` into its own parallel `web-preflight` job so the main `web` job could start `trunk build` immediately.

asi.hypothesis: `Web preflight` is a short node-only validation step on the current web critical path. Moving it into its own parallel job should preserve coverage while shaving a few seconds from the main web job’s wall time.
asi.root_cause_evidence: The candidate produced an implausibly large proxy win (`82s -> 26s`) because this is a workflow-dirty branch state with no exact runtime match, so the model fell back to fast local timings for the run steps while still using observed setup durations. That is precisely the remaining benchmark-quality gap around workflow-dirty candidates noted in the ideas file, not credible evidence of a real 56-second CI win.
asi.verification: Updated `.github/workflows/ci.yml` to add a parallel `web-preflight` job and remove `Web preflight` from the main `web` job, then reran `./autoresearch.sh`. The YAML parsed cleanly and the benchmark completed, but the resulting metric was too obviously artifact-driven to trust.
asi.rollback_reason: Do not spend a real CI run on a candidate whose projected improvement is clearly dominated by the workflow-dirty fallback model rather than believable step-level savings.
asi.next_action_hint: Let autoresearch revert this workflow draft, then improve the benchmark for workflow-dirty candidates—for example by reusing observed run-step durations when app/test runtime files still match even if the workflow topology changed. Re-evaluate the split-preflight idea only after that benchmark gap is closed.

description: Tried extending the proxy so workflow-dirty candidates can still reuse observed run-step durations when the app/test runtime files match the current branch state.

asi.hypothesis: Even when the workflow file changes and exact overall runtime matching is unavailable, the proxy should still be able to reuse observed durations for known run steps if the app/test runtime files themselves still match a set of successful CI runs.
asi.root_cause_evidence: The first validation attempt did not fail in the new matching logic itself; it hit another transient repeated `test:pw-legacy` benchmark failure before metrics were emitted. Recent manual reruns of the same legacy command have often passed immediately afterward, so this looks like the same flaky local benchmark behavior seen in earlier sessions rather than evidence against the benchmark-change hypothesis.
asi.rollback_reason: Cannot judge the benchmark-change candidate from this run because the repeated local legacy benchmark crashed before `./autoresearch.sh` could finish.
asi.next_action_hint: Let autoresearch revert this crash entry only in code-preserving files, reapply the workflow-dirty run-step matching change if needed, and rerun the same benchmark-improvement experiment. The next successful run should confirm whether workflow-dirty candidates can be modeled against observed run-step durations instead of unrealistically fast local timings.
asi.failure_detail: `run_experiment` failed inside the repeated local `pnpm run test:pw-legacy` benchmark command before the new workflow-dirty matching logic could produce output.

description: Extend the proxy so workflow-dirty candidates can still reuse observed run-step durations when the app/test runtime files match the current branch state.

asi.hypothesis: For workflow-dirty candidates, step-name matching alone is too weak but full exact-runtime matching is too strict. If the app/test runtime files still match successful CI runs, the proxy should reuse those observed run-step durations instead of dropping all the way to optimistic local timings.
asi.root_cause_evidence: After `af59406`, the proxy was realistic for exact current-branch matches (~82s vs ~87s actual), but workflow-dirty candidates like the split-preflight draft still collapsed to implausible ~26s because any workflow change disabled reuse of observed run-step durations and forced all known commands back to fast local timings. The missing middle ground was 'runtime-code exact, workflow dirty'.
asi.benchmark_change: `autoresearch.sh` now distinguishes three cases: (1) exact workflow + exact runtime match, which reuses observed per-job-step durations for everything; (2) workflow-dirty but runtime-code exact, which reuses observed run-step durations gathered from successful runs whose runtime files match the current branch while still modeling setup/topology through the existing workflow-aware path; and (3) no runtime-code exact match, which still falls back to local timings for known run steps.
asi.verification: The first attempt hit an unrelated transient legacy benchmark flake, but the preserved benchmark change then passed on rerun of `./autoresearch.sh`. The resulting projected metric for the current branch moved to `78s`, and the branch now has the machinery needed to evaluate workflow-dirty candidates like split-preflight without collapsing to unrealistically low local-only totals.
asi.next_action_hint: Re-evaluate the split-`web-preflight` candidate next under this improved benchmark. It was previously discarded specifically because the workflow-dirty fallback was too optimistic; this new model should give a much more credible signal.
